devon: heads-up — noticed steady mem growth on kv cache during longctx soak when prefix-reuse + session-stickiness are enabled. heap graph: https://ci.internal/heap/1768504321.png :thinking:

anna: ugh, do you have a repro? which flags exactly?

devon: quick repro: run longctx-load for ~2h with sticky_session=true and prefetch=true, cache_key = fingerprint(prefix || session_id || tenant). observed resident -> +1.2GB. logs: ```KVCache: store_count=1.2M, shard_frag=0.38, evict_calls=0```

michael: that cache_key shape stands out. including session_id will make keys explode across requests even for same prefix. looks like fragmentation rather than leak? :eyes:

sree: agree. if session_id is high-cardinality we lose reuse. we should canonicalize keys to prefix+tenant and have session-affinity metadata separate.

devon: interesting twist: when we flip sticky_session=false memory stabilizes but tail latency jumps for some customers. so sticky_session helps latency but hurts cache density. we're seeing both: worse reuse and more paging/evictions.

anna: any signal about batching heuristics interacting? e.g., large batch size causing different kernel path -> different activation shapes -> different prefixes?

michael: yes. profiling showed that when batching increases, we sometimes switch to the 'chunked-attn' kernel for long sequences which creates slightly different kv fingerprinting (we append seqlen marker). That marker is being included in the key in the current implementation. bug.

devon: exact culprit: in kv_key_builder we serialize a small header that includes runtime_mode and seqlen_mod. someone added seqlen_mod to avoid collisions, but it's too high-cardinality. patch attached: https://git.local/r/4321

sree: can we change to stable-slots: compute slot = hash(prefix) % N and only include slot in key? reduces cardinality while preserving safety. also tiered-eviction would help: prefer evict per-session slots before global prefix entries.

anna: +1 on slotting. also we should change default for sticky_session to 'affine' which keeps routing sticky on decision layer but doesn't bake session id into cache key. low-cost change.

michael: wrote a small perf test: run with slotting N=256 and sticky_session=affine -> reuse_rate goes from 0.12 -> 0.67 in our load test; mem growth gone in 2h run. flamegraph: https://ci.internal/flame/1768504412.svg

devon: nice. can someone open a PR for canonicalization + docs note about kernel flags not being part of key unless strictly necessary? I'll also add a longctx soak to our perf-suite.

deploy-bot: staging deploy queued: kv-key-canonicalizer branch -> staging (id: deploy-1768504700).

infra-bot: alert suppressed for kv-cache-oom-rule during test window (1768504320-1768506000).

sree: one more thing — add a metric for "key-cardinality-per-prefix" and an alert when it exceeds threshold. that will catch regressions earlier.

devon: will do. thanks all. next steps: PR for key canonicalization (devon), slotting perf run (michael), sticky_session defaults change proposal (anna).

anna: thanks. follow-up sync tomorrow 11am. :thumbsup:
